stem: Halogenoalkanes react with a number of different reagents in nucleophilic substitution reactions.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: A sample of potassium cyanide dissolved in ethanol is added to a sample of 1-bromobutane, $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{Br}$, and heated under reflux. A nucleophilic substitution reaction occurs and compound **A** is formed.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: What is meant by the term *nucleophile*?

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Identify the nucleophile in this reaction.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text: Explain why this reaction is described as a substitution reaction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: State the reagent(s) and conditions needed for $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{Br}$ to react to form $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{NH}_2$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
Equal amounts of three different halogenoalkanes are added to three separate test-tubes. An equal amount of aqueous silver nitrate and ethanol is added to each test-tube. The time taken for a precipitate to form is recorded for each halogenoalkane.

| halogenoalkane | time taken for precipitate to form/s |
| :--- | :--- |
| $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCl}$ | 460 |
| $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CBr}$ | 190 |
| $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CI}$ | 40 |

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Describe and explain the trend in reactivity of the different halogenoalkanes shown in this experiment.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
All three halogenoalkanes tend to react via the $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism.

Explain why the $\text{S}_\text{N}1$ mechanism is favoured.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Identify a halogenoalkane which tends to react with an aqueous solution of silver nitrate and ethanol via the $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism.
